Zod schema objects do not override toString, so both keys evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" (with the duplicate key having the last one win), meaning the 'minimum' schema effectively only validates `{ access_token }`. Zod's default behavior strips unrecognized keys, so in credential-sync mode fields like expiry_date/expires_in/instance_url are removed from the parsed data before callers (e.g. GoogleCalendarService spreads `token.data` into googleCredentials, Office365CalendarService spreads `tokenResponse.data`) persist it — so access token expiry is never updated and stale/malformed credentials get saved. The mechanism is fully verifiable in the diff and describes real incorrect behavior introduced by this change.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. In JS/TS, `z.string()` returns an object, and calling `.toString()` on it produces the literal string `"[object Object]"`, so both computed keys collapse to the same property name (and one overwrites the other). Zod `z.object()` also strips unknown keys by default, so in “sync mode” (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) the schema effectively only preserves `access_token` (plus possibly a `"[object Object]"` field), dropping `expiry_date`/`expires_in`/etc. This can lead to persisted credentials missing expiry data (e.g., Google/Office365/Zoom now call `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` before updating prisma), breaking token refresh behavior.
